text:
Alex K: Heads-up — ACME Prod reported a sudden p99 jump on short prompts for text.generate (short payloads only). Started ~03:10 PDT, p99 from ~450ms -> ~2.1s. No obvious errors in customer logs, just slow responses.
Priya M: oncall looking. which route/key/region? any recent config changes?
Alex K: Route=hosted-api:/v1/text.generate, region=us-west-2, customer uses small prompts (~10-50 tokens). We rolled batcher config change yesterday (cfg-batcher-2026-03-16) that increased coalesce/grace for micro-traffic to improve throughput.
Samir R: thx. Possible we increased the grace window so small reqs wait longer until batch fills. That trades latency for cost. Can you dump batcher metrics for that route?
Alex K: grabbing metrics now — snippet from internal metrics API:
```
# metrics query: batcher_wait_ms{route="/v1/text.generate",env="prod"}
p50=8.2, p95=120.4, p99=2100.7
batch_size_p95=1.0, batch_size_p99=2.0
active_batches=18
```
Notable: p99 wait ~2.1s and batch sizes at p99 are tiny (1-2) — suggests long wait for late arrivals.
Jamie L: customer also mentioned some 401s earlier but they retried; auth looks separate. main pain is latency.
Priya M: can you also paste the batcher config for that tier? especially `hold_ms`, `max_wait_ms`, `grace_window` and routing policy.
Alex K: current config (applied yesterday):
```
continuous_batcher:
  hold_ms: 12
  max_batch_size: 64
  min_coalesce_ms: 6
  grace_window_ms: 200
  prefer_latency: false
```
We increased min_coalesce_ms/grace_window to reduce tiny batches.
Samir R: yep — that `grace_window_ms: 200` + min_coalesce of 6 means low-volume tiny requests sometimes sit waiting for coalescing heuristics then hit max_wait causing big tail. For short prompts tiny compute time makes waiting dominate.
Samir R: immediate mitigation options: 1) set prefer_latency=true for that route (bypass longer coalesce), 2) drop grace_window_ms to 10 for short-payload routes, 3) add latency-only override that forces eager flush when predicted batch size < X.
Priya M: which is least risky for prod?
Samir R: prefer_latency=true is safe and reversible; it will prefer smaller batches and lower wait. We'll quantize cost impact but ok for a customer-facing canary.
Alex K: can we hotpatch that on the route?
Samir R: yes — PR ready: `infra/patches/2026-03-16-batcher-override` — applying to a small subset first.
deploy-bot: Config patch `batcher-route-override-prefer-latency` was deployed to canary (hosts: us-west-2-a) by Samir R at 2800001300.
Samir R: repro command (to simulate tiny prompts):
```
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/text.generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -d '{"input":"hi"}' &
  sleep 0.01
done
```
Run from a few clients to mimic bursty tiny traffic.
Alex K: ran canary repro — results after patch:
```
p50=9.1ms, p95=86.7ms, p99=482.3ms
batch_size_p95=1.0, batch_size_p99=1.0
```
Huge improvement on p99 for small payloads.
Jamie L: customer confirmed latency dropped after our config change. They still saw a handful of auth retries earlier but not a blocker.
Priya M: cool. Next steps: 1) roll prefer_latency override to all hosts in us-west-2 for short-payload route (low-risk), 2) file follow-up to instrument `batcher_wait_ms` alert for p99>500ms for short-req routes, 3) add a regression test in perf-suite that simulates tiny prompt bursts.
Samir R: i'm scheduling a gradual rollout and will monitor cost delta. I'll also add a fine-grained flag `min_latency_mode` so we can target only routes that care about latency.
Alex K: +1. Please note in ticket 4528 (ACME-prod latency) and tag eng-platform for a config UI to make this override easier. :thumbsup: 
Priya M: closing the immediate escalation — will keep watch for 2h then update postmortem owners. Thanks everyone.
Samir R: thanks — adding scoreboard note about the accidental coalesce/grace tradeoff.
deploy-bot: Rolled out prefer-latency flag to us-west-2 (all hosts) at 2800001360 — monitor metrics: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abcd/batcher?from=now-2h
Alex K: confirmed customer p99 steady ~470-520ms now. Marking incident mitigated.
Priya M: filing doc & postmortem link to ticket 4528. If anyone sees regressions ping me.
